event.canonical_title: Trump Announces Deal for Hamas Disarmament and Israeli Withdrawal from Gaza
event.summary: President Trump has announced a deal for Hamas to completely disarm, which includes the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. Hamas confirmed its agreement to the plan, stating it would hand over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee. However, the implementation of this deal is contingent upon Israel fulfilling its commitments from a previous agreement.

timeline.title: Israeli Military Actions Challenge Trump's Gaza Peace Proposal
timeline.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected a recent peace proposal from US President Donald Trump, which calls for the disarmament of Hamas and an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza. Netanyahu stated that the Israeli army will not retreat from its positions until Hamas is fully disarmed, contradicting the terms of a previous ceasefire agreement. Meanwhile, reports indicate that Trump would be disappointed if Israel does not accept the new plan.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.subject: Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Peace Deal refers to the U.S.-backed, internationally supported framework to end the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza through a ceasefire, hostage and detainee releases, Hamas’s disarmament and Gaza’s demilitarization, Israeli withdrawals tied to agreed milestones, humanitarian access, and postwar governance and reconstruction. It builds on earlier Egypt-, Qatar-, and U.S.-mediated ceasefire efforts, but its implementation depends on compliance and verification by multiple parties rather than on a single self-executing agreement.

facts.label: Framework and international status
facts.value: President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan is a 20-point roadmap; the United Nations Security Council endorsed the plan in Resolution 2803 (2025) and welcomed a Board of Peace to support its implementation.

facts.label: Core proposed exchange and military step
facts.value: The framework envisages an end to military operations and a staged Israeli withdrawal, alongside the return of hostages and the release of specified Palestinian detainees; further withdrawal is linked to agreed demilitarization standards, milestones, and timeframes.

facts.label: Disarmament and transitional governance
facts.value: A subsequent 15-point implementation roadmap, presented by Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, the United States, and the High Representative for Gaza, calls for Hamas to end military, policing, and administrative activity and for the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to serve as the transitional civilian authority.

facts.label: Institutions and outside roles
facts.value: The plan’s implementation architecture includes the Board of Peace, an Office of the High Representative for Gaza, the NCAG, and an International Stabilization Force intended to support security, demilitarization, aid delivery, and reconstruction. Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, and the United States are identified as guarantors in the UN implementation report.

facts.label: Legal and humanitarian context
facts.value: The International Committee of the Red Cross considers Gaza occupied territory under its effective-control assessment and states that international humanitarian law continues to govern protections for civilians and duties relevant to the territory’s administration and supply.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows reported late-July to mid-August 2026 developments concerning the deal’s implementation, Israeli-Hamas military and political responses, and one related Lebanon escalation; it is not a complete chronology of the Gaza war, all negotiations, humanitarian conditions, or the wider regional conflict.
